{{Short description|German planetary scientist}}
[[File:Gneukum.jpg|thumb|right|Gerhard Neukum at Free University of Berlin.]]
'''Gerhard Neukum''' (1944-2014) was a German planetary scientist who worked on the chronology of solar system bodies.  He obtained a Ph.D. in physics at [[Heidelberg University]]. He was a professor at [[LMU Munich]] and at the [[Free University of Berlin]].<ref name=AAS>[https://dps.aas.org/news/gerhard-neukum-1944-2014#:~:text=Gerhard%20Neukum%2C%20our%20planetary%20scientist,recognised%20experts%20in%20the%20field. Gerhard Neukum 1944-2014], biographical note at American Astronomical Society</ref>

Neukum was involved in the ESA [[Mars Express]] mission, the joint ESA-NASA [[Cassini–Huygens]] mission, the ESA [[Rosetta (spacecraft)|Rosetta]] mission, and the NASA [[Dawn (spacecraft)|Dawn]] mission.<ref name=AAS/> He also led a consortium of scientists in developing the first proposal for a [[Mercury (planet)|Mercury]] orbiter spacecraft, submitted to [[ESA]] in 1985.<ref name="Benkhoff2021">{{cite journal |last1=Benkhoff |first1=J. |last2=Murakami |first2=G. |last3=Baumjohann |first3=W. |last4=Besse |first4=S. |last5=Bunce |first5=E. |last6=Casale |first6=M. |last7=Cremosese |first7=G. |last8=Glassmeier |first8=K.-H. |last9=Hayakawa |first9=H. |last10=Heyner |first10=D. |last11=Hiesinger |first11=H. |last12=Huovelin |first12=J. |last13=Hussmann |first13=H. |last14=Iafolla |first14=V. |last15=Iess |first15=L. |last16=Kasaba |first16=Y. |last17=Kobayashi |first17=M. |last18=Milillo |first18=A. |last19=Mitrofanov |first19=I. G. |last20=Montagnon |first20=E. |last21=Novara |first21=M. |last22=Orsini |first22=S. |last23=Quemerais |first23=E. |last24=Reininghaus |first24=U. |last25=Saito |first25=Y. |last26=Santoli |first26=F. |last27=Stramaccioni |first27=D. |last28=Sutherland |first28=O. |last29=Thomas |first29=N. |last30=Yoshikawa |first30=I. |last31=Zender |first31=J. |title=BepiColombo - Mission Overview and Science Goals |journal=Space Science Reviews |date=December 2021 |volume=217 |issue=8 |doi=10.1007/s11214-021-00861-4 |display-authors=3 |hdl=10138/337997 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Balogh2007">{{cite journal |last1=Balogh |first1=André |last2=Grard |first2=Réjean |last3=Solomon |first3=Sean C. |last4=Schulz |first4=Rita |last5=Langevin |first5=Yves |last6=Kasaba |first6=Yasumasa |last7=Fujimoto |first7=Masaki |title=Missions to Mercury |journal=Space Science Reviews |date=October 2007 |volume=132 |issue=2-4 |pages=611–645 |doi=10.1007/s11214-007-9212-4 |display-authors=3}}</ref>

The [[List of minor planets: 6001–7000#150|asteroid 6150]] was named after Neukum.

The crater [[Neukum (Martian crater)|Neukum]] on [[Mars (planet)|Mars]] was named after him by the [[International Astronomical Union|IAU]] in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url = http://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/15687 |title = Neukum |publisher = [[NASA]] |work = Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature |accessdate = 29 June 2020}}</ref>
